_note: THE MASTER LEGEND. Every map merges this, then may override single glyphs. design/11-map-data.md authors maps as ASCII grids; this is the key those grids are read against, and the only place a colour or a movement cost is decided.
_detail: The `detail` field is a RENDERING instruction, not a rule. It tells hexmap.js what to scatter inside the hex — grass tufts, plough furrows, tree canopies, hill hachures — so that country reads as country instead of as a coloured tile. The scatter is hashed from the hex coordinate, so it is identical on thirty screens and stable across every redraw.

..name: plaza
..about: Packed bare earth. Gonzales had seven public squares; this is the one the town actually used.

'.name: prairie
'.about: Open grass. It runs from the last house to the treeline.

c.name: corn stubble
c.about: The corn is already in. What is left is knee-high and dry.

o.name: orchard
o.about: Planted trees in rows. You can see between them.

\".name: brush
\".about: Mesquite and thorn. Slow, and you cannot see through it.

t.name: scattered trees
t.about: A few big trees standing in the open.

T.name: timber
T.about: Bottomland timber — pecan, cottonwood, post oak. Heavy going.

w.name: cane
w.about: Cane brake along the water. Over your head.

^.name: rise
^.about: High ground. Costs to climb, and you can see from it.

=.name: road
=.about: A wagon road. Riders move down it for free.

-.name: path
-.about: A footpath worn between two places people go.

x.name: pen
x.about: A rail-fenced lot. Stock, or a garden somebody is protecting.

#.name: building
#.about: A house, a store, a shop. You go IN through the door, not through the wall.

A.name: adobe
A.about: Thick mud-brick walls. Cool inside, and hard to shoot through.

j.name: jacal
j.about: Upright poles, mud packed between, thatched roof. Most of Béxar lived in one.

W.name: wall
W.about: You do not go through a wall. Find the gate.

y.name: courtyard
y.about: Enclosed open ground inside the walls.

R.name: rubble
R.about: Fallen stone. Slow, but it will stop a ball.

~.name: river
~.about: The Guadalupe. You do not walk across it. Find the ford.

a.name: acequia
a.about: An irrigation ditch. Waist deep and awkward, but you can get over it.

f.name: ford
f.about: Where the river runs shallow enough to cross. Everybody knows where it is.

B.name: bridge
B.about: Planks over the water. One at a time.

b.name: riverbank
b.about: The strip between the water and the grass.

s.name: sandbar
s.about: Dry gravel the river left behind.

_.name: floor
_.about: Inside. Puncheon floor, or beaten dirt.

d.name: dirt floor
d.about: Swept dirt. Most floors in Texas in 1835.

h.name: hearth
h.about: The fireplace. Light, heat, and where the cooking happens.

F.name: forge
F.about: The smith's fire, and the bellows beside it.

n.name: furniture
n.about: A counter, a table, shelves, barrels. Climb over it if you must.

D.name: doorway
D.about: The way in, and the way out.

P.name: breezeway
P.about: The open passage through the middle of a dogtrot house. Shade, and a draught.

L.name: ladder
L.about: Up to the loft, where people sleep.

M.name: metate
M.about: The sloped stone where corn is ground, by hand, every single day.

N.name: niche
N.about: A hollow in a wall ten inches thick. A santo, and a candle.

light._note: What the map looks like at each hour, and in each weather. design/12 sets the tone; this sets the tint. A student should be able to tell what time it is WITHOUT reading a word.
